nodes.name: Generalisation of Lemma 11 to chains
nodes.statement: Let $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2 \supset \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1 \supset H_0$ be a sequence of strongly connected reflexive tournaments, each one a subtournament of the one before. Suppose that any endomorphism of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1$ that fixes $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ is an automorphism. Then any endomorphism $h$ of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2$ that maps $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ to an isomorphic copy $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0=i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$ of itself also gives an isomorphic copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1$ in $h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1)$.
assumptions: Let $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2 \supset \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1 \supset H_0$ be a sequence of strongly connected reflexive tournaments, each one a subtournament of the one before.
Suppose that any endomorphism of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1$ that fixes $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ is an automorphism.
conclusions: any endomorphism $h$ of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2$ that maps $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ to an isomorphic copy $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0=i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$ of itself also gives an isomorphic copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1$ in $h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1)$.
nodes.label: lem:8

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 13
nodes.statement: For contradiction, suppose there is an endomorphism $h$ of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2$ that maps $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ to an isomorphic copy $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0=i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$ of itself that does not yield an isomorphic copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1$. In particular, $|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1)|<|V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1)|$. We proceed as in the proof of the Lemma~\ref{lem:7}. Choose $h^{-1}$ in the following fashion. We let $h^{-1}$ of $h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$ be the natural isomorphism of $h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ (that inverts the isomorphism given by $h$ from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0$). Otherwise we choose $h^{-1}$ arbitrarily, such that $h^{-1}(y)=x$ only if $h(x)=y$. Since $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2$ is a reflexive tournament, $h^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. And $h^{-1} \circ h$ is an endomorphism of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2$ that fixes $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ that does not yield an isomorphic copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1$ in $h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1)$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: As for Lemma 11: compose with a chosen inverse to get an endomorphism fixing H_0 that collapses H_1, a contradiction.

nodes.name: Assume H_1 collapses
nodes.statement: For contradiction, suppose there is an endomorphism $h$ of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2$ that maps $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ to an isomorphic copy $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0=i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$ of itself that does not yield an isomorphic copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1$. In particular, $|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1)|<|V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1)|$.
nodes.statement_short: Suppose h does not give an isomorphic copy of H_1.

nodes.name: Choose an inverse as in Lemma 11
nodes.statement: We proceed as in the proof of the Lemma~\ref{lem:7}. Choose $h^{-1}$ in the following fashion. We let $h^{-1}$ of $h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$ be the natural isomorphism of $h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ (that inverts the isomorphism given by $h$ from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0$). Otherwise we choose $h^{-1}$ arbitrarily, such that $h^{-1}(y)=x$ only if $h(x)=y$.
nodes.statement_short: As in Lemma 11, choose h^{-1} inverting h on H_0.

nodes.name: Contradiction
nodes.statement: Since $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2$ is a reflexive tournament, $h^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. And $h^{-1} \circ h$ is an endomorphism of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2$ that fixes $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ that does not yield an isomorphic copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1$ in $h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1)$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: h^{-1}h fixes H_0 but collapses H_1, contradiction.

nodes.name: General Case I
nodes.statement: Let $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{0},\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{1}, \ldots, \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k, \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ be reflexive tournaments, the first $k$ of which have Hamilton cycles $\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{0},\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{1}, \ldots, \ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{k}$, respectively, so that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0 \subseteq H_1 \subseteq \cdots \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}.$ Assume that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$, $(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1,\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$, \ldots, $(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k},\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k-1})$ are endo-trivial and that \[ \begin{array}{lcl} \mathrm{Spill}_{a_0}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0,\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{0}]) &= &V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1) \\ \mathrm{Spill}_{a_1}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1,\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{1}]) &= &V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2) \\ \hspace*{3mm} \vdots &\vdots &\hspace*{3mm}\vdots \\ \mathrm{Spill}_{a_{k-1}}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k-1},\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{k-1}]) &= &V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k).\\ \end{array} \] Assume that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ retracts to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$ and also to every isomorphic copy $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_{k}=i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k)$ of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ with $\mathrm{Spill}_{a_k}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_k,i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{k})]) = V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1})$. Then $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$-{\sc Retraction} can be polynomially reduced to {\sc Surjective $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$-Colouring}.
assumptions: Let $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{0},\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{1}, \ldots, \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k, \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ be reflexive tournaments, the first $k$ of which have Hamilton cycles $\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{0},\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{1}, \ldots, \ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{k}$, respectively, so that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0 \subseteq H_1 \subseteq \cdots \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}.$

Assume that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$, $(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1,\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$, \ldots, $(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k},\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k-1})$ are endo-trivial and that \[ \begin{array}{lcl} \mathrm{Spill}_{a_0}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0,\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{0}]) &= &V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1) \\ \mathrm{Spill}_{a_1}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1,\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{1}]) &= &V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2) \\ \hspace*{3mm} \vdots &\vdots &\hspace*{3mm}\vdots \\ \mathrm{Spill}_{a_{k-1}}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k-1},\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{k-1}]) &= &V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k).\\ \end{array} \]

Assume that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ retracts to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$ and also to every isomorphic copy $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_{k}=i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k)$ of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ with $\mathrm{Spill}_{a_k}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_k,i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{k})]) = V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1})$.
conclusions: $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$-{\sc Retraction} can be polynomially reduced to {\sc Surjective $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$-Colouring}.
nodes.statement_short: For a chain H_0 in ... in H_{k+1} with endo-trivial pairs and full Spills, if H_{k+1} retracts to all suitable copies of H_k then H_k-Retraction reduces to Surjective H_{k+1}-Colouring.
nodes.label: prop:main-general1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 14 (General Case I)
nodes.statement: Let $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ be an instance of {\sc $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$-Retraction}. We will build an instance $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$ of {\sc Surjective $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$-Colouring} in the following fashion. First, take a copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ together with $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ and build $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$ by identifying these on the copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k}$ that they both possess as a subgraph. We now build $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$ as follows. First we augment $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$ with a new copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*}_{a_k}$ for every vertex $v\in V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}')\setminus V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k)$. Vertex~$v$ is to be identified with any vertex in the top copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}}^*_{a_k}$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*}_{a_k}$, and the bottom copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}}^*_{a_k}$ is to be identified with $\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_k$ according to the identity function. Then, for each $i \in [k+1]$, and $v \in V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{i}) \setminus V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{i-1})$, add a copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*}_{a_{i-1}}$, where $v$ is identified with any vertex in the top copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}}^*_{a_{i-1}}$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*}_{a_{i-1}}$ and the bottom copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}}^*_{i-1}$ is to be identified with $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{i-1}$ according to the identity map of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}}^*_{a_{i-1}}$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{i-1}$. We claim that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ retracts to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$ if and only if there exists a surjective homomorphism from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$. First suppose that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ retracts to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$. Let $h$ be a retraction from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k}$. Extend $h$ mapping $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ according to the identity to ensure the final mapping is surjective. Finally, we map the various copies of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*}_{a_{i-1}}$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$ in any suitable fashion, which will always exist due to our assumptions and the fact that $\mathrm{Spill}_{a_{k}}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k},\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{k}]) = V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1})$, which follows from our assumption that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ retracts to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:spillage}. Now suppose that if there exists a surjective homomorphism~$h$ from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$. Suppose that $|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)|=1$. Then $|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*}_{a_0})|=1$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:claim1}. Now we follow the chain of spills to deduce that $|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1})|=1$, which is not possible. Now, $1<|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)|<a_0$ is not possible either due to Lemma~\ref{lem:under-m}. Thus, $|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)|=|V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)|$ and indeed $h$ maps $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ to a copy of itself in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ which we will call $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0=i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$. We now apply Lemma~\ref{lem:8} as well as our assumed endo-trivialities to derive that $h$ in fact maps $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$ by the isomorphism $i$ to a copy of itself in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ which we will call $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_{k}$. Since $h$ is surjective, we can deduce that $\mathrm{Spill}_{a_k}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_k,i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{k})]) = V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1})$ in the same way as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{prop:main1}. and so there exists a retraction $r$ from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_k$. Now $i^{-1} \circ r \circ h$ gives the desired retraction of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$.
nodes.statement_short: Recursive gadget reduction as in Base Case I, with gadgets attached along the chain; Lemma 13 propagates injectivity from H_0 to H_k.

nodes.name: Glue H_{k+1} to the instance
nodes.statement: Let $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ be an instance of {\sc $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$-Retraction}. We will build an instance $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$ of {\sc Surjective $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$-Colouring} in the following fashion. First, take a copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ together with $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ and build $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$ by identifying these on the copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k}$ that they both possess as a subgraph.
nodes.statement_short: Form G' by gluing H_{k+1} and G along H_k.

nodes.name: Attach gadgets
nodes.statement: We now build $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$ as follows. First we augment $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$ with a new copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*}_{a_k}$ for every vertex $v\in V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}')\setminus V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k)$. Vertex~$v$ is to be identified with any vertex in the top copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}}^*_{a_k}$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*}_{a_k}$, and the bottom copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}}^*_{a_k}$ is to be identified with $\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_k$ according to the identity function. Then, for each $i \in [k+1]$, and $v \in V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{i}) \setminus V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{i-1})$, add a copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*}_{a_{i-1}}$, where $v$ is identified with any vertex in the top copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}}^*_{a_{i-1}}$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*}_{a_{i-1}}$ and the bottom copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}}^*_{i-1}$ is to be identified with $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{i-1}$ according to the identity map of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}}^*_{a_{i-1}}$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{i-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Attach gadgets at vertices outside H_k and along the chain.

nodes.name: Claim: reduction is correct
nodes.statement: We claim that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ retracts to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$ if and only if there exists a surjective homomorphism from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: State the equivalence.

nodes.name: Forward direction
nodes.statement: First suppose that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ retracts to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$. Let $h$ be a retraction from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k}$. Extend $h$ mapping $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ according to the identity to ensure the final mapping is surjective. Finally, we map the various copies of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*}_{a_{i-1}}$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$ in any suitable fashion, which will always exist due to our assumptions and the fact that $\mathrm{Spill}_{a_{k}}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k},\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{k}]) = V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1})$, which follows from our assumption that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ retracts to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:spillage}.
nodes.statement_short: Extend the retraction using the Spill assumptions and Lemma 9.

nodes.name: Backward direction: H_0 not collapsed
nodes.statement: Now suppose that if there exists a surjective homomorphism~$h$ from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$. Suppose that $|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)|=1$. Then $|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*}_{a_0})|=1$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:claim1}. Now we follow the chain of spills to deduce that $|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1})|=1$, which is not possible.
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 8 and the chain of spills, |h(H_0)|=1 is impossible.

nodes.name: Rule out partial collapse
nodes.statement: Now, $1<|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)|<a_0$ is not possible either due to Lemma~\ref{lem:under-m}.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 7 rules out 1<|h(H_0)|<a_0.

nodes.name: Propagate the isomorphism
nodes.statement: Thus, $|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)|=|V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)|$ and indeed $h$ maps $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ to a copy of itself in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ which we will call $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0=i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$. We now apply Lemma~\ref{lem:8} as well as our assumed endo-trivialities to derive that $h$ in fact maps $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$ by the isomorphism $i$ to a copy of itself in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ which we will call $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_{k}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 13 and the endo-trivialities give h maps H_k isomorphically.

nodes.name: Obtain the retraction
nodes.statement: Since $h$ is surjective, we can deduce that $\mathrm{Spill}_{a_k}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_k,i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{k})]) = V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1})$ in the same way as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{prop:main1}. and so there exists a retraction $r$ from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_k$. Now $i^{-1} \circ r \circ h$ gives the desired retraction of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k$.
nodes.statement_short: As in Lemma 10, Spill is full, so H_{k+1} retracts to H'_k, giving the retraction.

nodes.name: General Case II
nodes.statement: Let $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{0},\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{1}, \ldots, \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k, \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ be reflexive tournaments, the first $k+1$ of which have Hamilton cycles $\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{0},\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{1}, \ldots, \ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{k}$, respectively, so that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0 \subseteq H_1 \subseteq \cdots \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$. Suppose that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$, $(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1,\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$, \ldots, $(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k},\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k-1}), (\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1},\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k})$ are endo-trivial and that \[ \begin{array}{lcl} \mathrm{Spill}_{a_0}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0,\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{0}]) &= &V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1) \\ \mathrm{Spill}_{a_1}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1,\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{1}]) &= &V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2) \\ \hspace*{3mm} \vdots &\vdots &\hspace*{3mm}\vdots \\ \mathrm{Spill}_{a_{k-1}}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k-1},\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{k-1}]) &= &V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k)\\ \mathrm{Spill}_{a_{k}}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k},\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{k}]) &= &V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}) \end{array} \] Then {\sc $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$-Retraction} can be polynomially reduced to {\sc Surjective $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$-Colouring}.

Suppose that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$, $(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1,\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$, \ldots, $(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k},\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k-1}), (\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1},\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k})$ are endo-trivial and that \[ \begin{array}{lcl} \mathrm{Spill}_{a_0}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0,\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{0}]) &= &V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1) \\ \mathrm{Spill}_{a_1}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1,\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{1}]) &= &V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_2) \\ \hspace*{3mm} \vdots &\vdots &\hspace*{3mm}\vdots \\ \mathrm{Spill}_{a_{k-1}}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k-1},\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{k-1}]) &= &V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_k)\\ \mathrm{Spill}_{a_{k}}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k},\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{k}]) &= &V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}) \end{array} \]

nodes.statement_short: For a chain of reflexive tournaments with endo-trivial pairs (including the top pair) and full Spills, H_{k+1}-Retraction reduces to Surjective H_{k+1}-Colouring.
nodes.label: prop:main-general2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 15 (General Case II)
nodes.statement: Let $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ be an instance of {\sc $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$-Retraction}. We build an instance $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$ of {\sc Surjective $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$-Colouring} in the following fashion. Build $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$ by, for each $i \in [k+1]$, and $v \in V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{i}) \setminus V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{i-1})$, adding a copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*}_{a_{i-1}}$, where $v$ is identified with any vertex in the top copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}}^*_{a_{i-1}}$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*}_{a_{i-1}}$ and the bottom copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}}^*_{i-1}$ is to be identified with $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{i-1}$ according to the identity map of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}}^*_{a_{i-1}}$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_{i-1}$. We claim that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ retracts to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$ if and only if there exists a surjective homomorphism from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$. First suppose that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ retracts to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$. Let $h$ be a retraction from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$. Then we can extend $h$ by mapping $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$ in some suitable fashion, which is possible due to the spill assumptions. Now suppose that there exists a surjective homomorphism~$h$ from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1}$. Suppose that $|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)|=1$. Then $|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*}_{a_0})|=1$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:claim1}. Now we follow the chain of spills to deduce that $|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_{k+1})|=1$, a contradiction. nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3
nodes.statement: As $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ is is a strongly connected reflexive tournament, which has more than one vertex by our definition, $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ is not transitive. Note that {\sc $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$-Retraction} is \ensuremath{\mathsf{NP}}-complete, since non-transitive reflexive tournaments omit Taylor polymorphisms~\cite{larose2006taylor}, following Theorem~\ref{thm:ret-hardness}. Thus, if $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ is endo-trivial, the result follows from Lemma~\ref{prop:main1} (note that we could also have used Corollary~\ref{c-main}). Suppose $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ is not endo-trivial. Then, by Lemma~\ref{lem:endo-retraction-trivial}, $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ is not retract-trivial either. This means $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ has a non-trivial retraction to some subtournament~$\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$. We may assume that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ is endo-trivial, as otherwise we will repeat the argument until we find a retraction from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ to an endo-trivial subtournament. If $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ retracts to all isomorphic copies $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0=i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$ of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ within it, except possibly those for which $\mathrm{Spill}_m(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0,i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_0)]) \neq V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}})$, then the result follows from Lemma~\ref{prop:main1}. So there is a copy $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0=i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0)$ to which $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ does not retract for which $\mathrm{Spill}_m(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0,i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_0)]) = V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}})$. If $(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}},\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0)$ is endo-trivial, the result follows from Lemma~\ref{prop:main2}. Thus we assume $(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}},\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0)$ is not endo-trivial and we deduce the existence of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0 \subset \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1 \subset \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ ($\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1$ is strictly between $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ and $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0$) so that $(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1,\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0)$ is endotrivial and $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ retracts to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1$. Now we are ready to break out. Either $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ retracts to all isomorphic copies of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_1=i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_1)$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$, except possibly for those so that $\mathrm{Spill}_m(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_1,i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_1)]) \neq V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}})$, and we apply Lemma~\ref{prop:main-general1}, or there exists a copy $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_1$, with $\mathrm{Spill}_m(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_1,i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_1)]) = V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}})$, to which it does not retract. Then $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_1$ contains $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}''_0$ a copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}''_0$ so that $(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_1,\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}''_0)$ and $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}''_0$ are endo-trivial. We now continue iterating this method, which will terminate because our structures are getting strictly larger.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4
nodes.statement: For strongly connected tournaments, the result follows from Corollary~\ref{cor:strongly-connected1}. Let $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ instead have $k>1$ strongly connected components $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}(1),\ldots,\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}(k)$. Since $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ is not transitive, one of these strongly connected components, $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}(i)$, must be of size greater than $1$, whereupon we know from Corollary~\ref{cor:strongly-connected2} that {\sc Surjective $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}(i)$-Colouring} is \ensuremath{\mathsf{NP}}-complete, even when restricted to strongly connected inputs. Let us reduce {\sc Surjective $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}(i)$-Colouring} to {\sc Surjective $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$-Colouring} by taking a strongly connected input $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ for the former and building $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$ by adding a copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ restricted to $V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}(1)),\ldots,V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}(i-1))$, where every vertex here has an edge to every vertex of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$, and adding a copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ restricted to $V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}(i+1)),\ldots,V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}(k))$, where every vertex there has an edge from every vertex of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$. Note that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$ has $k$ strongly connected components $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'(1),\ldots, \ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'(k)$, where $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'(h)$ is isomorphic to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'(h)$ for $h=1,\ldots,k$, $h\neq i$. We claim that there exists a surjective homomorphism from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}(i)$ if and only if there exists a surjective homomorphism from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$. (Forwards.) Map the additional vertices in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$ in the obvious fashion (by the ``identity'') to extend a surjective homomorphism from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_i$ so that it is surjective from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$. (Backwards.) In any surjective homomorphism $s$ from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$, we have that $s(V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'(i))) \subseteq V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}(i))$ for $i=1,\ldots k$.

nodes.statement: Consider the homomorphism $\varphi: \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}^n \rightarrow \ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}^{\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}}$ induced by an $n+1$-ary polymorphism of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ where $n \geq 1$; suppose for a contradiction that the polymorphism depends on all its variables. nodes.name: Claim 0 block

nodes.name: Claim 1 block

Similarly $(f,1)\in E(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}^{\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}})$ implies $f(i) \in \{0,1\}$ for all $i$ so (b) follows immediately. To prove (a), observe that any in- or out-neighbour of a constant cannot be surjective since no constant has in- or out-neighbourhood of size 3. For (c), argue again as we just did: $(1,f) \in E(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}^{\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}})$ means $f(i) \in \{1,2\}$ for all $i$, and $(f,1)\in E(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}^{\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}})$ implies $f(i) \in \{0,1\}$ for all $i$ and hence $f=1$; the proof for $c=2$ is identical.

nodes.name: Image of the looped part W
nodes.statement: Obviously the loops of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}^n$ are precisely the tuples whose coordinates belong to $\{1,2\}$. Call the subdigraph induced by these vertices $\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}}$, and notice it is weakly connected. Then the homomorphism $\varphi$ must map $\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}}$ onto a weakly connected digraph consisting of loops only. By Claim 1 (a) either (i) $\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}}$ is entirely mapped to $\{id\}$ or (ii) $\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}}$ is mapped by $\varphi$ to the set $\{1,2\}$.
nodes.statement_short: By Claim 1(a), W maps entirely to id or into the constants {1,2}.

nodes.name: Tuples with a zero coordinate
nodes.statement: Choose any tuple $X$ of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}^n$ containing a coordinate equal to 0. Then there exist $Y, Z \in W$ such that $(X,Z), (Z,Y), (Y,X) \in E(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}^n)$: indeed, let $Z$ be obtained from $X$ by replacing each 0 entry by 1, fixing all other coordinates, and let $Y$ be obtained from $X$ by replacing each 0 entry by 2, fixing all other coordinates.
nodes.statement_short: For X with a 0 entry build Y, Z in W forming a directed triangle with X.

nodes.name: Case (i)
nodes.statement: Thus in case (i) we get that $id = \varphi(Y), (\varphi(Y),\varphi(X)),(\varphi(X),\varphi(Z)) \in E(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}^{\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}})$ and $\varphi(Z)=id$ so by Claim 2 $\varphi$ maps all of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}^n$ to $id$.
nodes.statement_short: Claim 2 forces everything to map to id.

nodes.name: Case (ii)
nodes.statement: In case (ii), we get that $\varphi(Y)$ and $\varphi(Z)$ belong to $\{1,2\}$; since $(\varphi(Z),\varphi(Y))\in E(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}^{\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}})$ we must in fact have that $(\varphi(Z),\varphi(Y))$ belongs to $\{(1,1),(1,2),(2,2)\}$; thus we get one of the following cases, namely $(1,\varphi(X)),(\varphi(X),1) \in E(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}^{\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}})$ or $(1,\varphi(X)),(\varphi(X),2) \in E(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}^{\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}})$ or $(2,\varphi(X)),(\varphi(X),2) \in E(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}^{\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}})$. By Claim 1 (b) and (c) $\varphi(X)$ must be one of the constant maps 0, 1 or 2.
nodes.statement_short: Claims 1(b),(c) force phi(X) to be a constant.

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: Thus we conclude that $\varphi$ either maps all of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}^n$ to $\{id\}$, in which case our polymorphism cannot depend on its first $n$ variables; or otherwise $\varphi$ maps all of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}^n$ to constant maps, and then the polymorphism does not depend on its last variable, also a contradiction.

nodes.statement: As discussed, we only need to settle the complexity of {\sc $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$-Retraction} and {\sc Surjective $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$-Colouring} for the digraphs depicted in Figure~\ref{fig:3digraphs}, as for all other partially reflexive digraphs of size at most $3$, {\sc List $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$-Colouring} is in P \cite{FederHellTucker}. nodes.name: Why DC*_3 is the closest digraph analogue of 3-No-Rainbow-Colouring
nodes.statement: The {\sc Surjective $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}}^*_3$-Colouring} problem is the digraph problem most closely related to {\sc $3$-No-Rainbow-Colouring}. To explain this, when looking for digraphs with a similar character to $3\mathrm{NRC}$, we would insist at least that the automorphism group is transitive. This leaves just the reflexive and irreflexive directed $3$-cycles and the reflexive and irreflexive 3-cliques, that is, $3$-cycles with a double edge between every pair of vertices (admittedly, the cycles have only some of the automorphisms of the cliques). If~$\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ is the reflexive $3$-clique, then $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$-{\sc Retraction} and {\sc Surjective $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$-Colouring} are trivial. If~$\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ is the irreflexive directed $3$-cycle, then $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ has a majority polymorphism, which shows that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$-{\sc Retraction}, and thus {\sc Surjective $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$-Colouring} (see Figure~\ref{fig:Anthony}), can be solved in polynomial time~\cite{Semicomplete}. If~$\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ is the irreflexive $3$-clique, then {\sc Surjective $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$-Colouring} is \ensuremath{\mathsf{NP}}-complete, as there exists a straightforward reduction from 3-{\sc Colouring}. Hence~$\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}=\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}}^*_3$ was indeed the only case for which determining the complexity of {\sc Surjective $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$-Colouring} was not immediately obvious.
nodes.statement_short: Among digraphs with transitive automorphism group on 3 vertices, all cases but the reflexive directed 3-cycle are easy to classify.
